faqs.q: Sec. 102-62.1. - Water meter pit or vault access standards.
faqs.a:
(a)
City personnel performing inspection, servicing, repair, removal, or replacement of
               water meters, water meter vaults, or water meter pits shall have access to the property
               served by the city water system as provided in this section.
(b)
For routine servicing of water meter vaults, a property owner receiving water service
               shall maintain an area, accessible from the public right of way, over and above the
               meter vault encompassing a surface area measured six feet outward from the center
               of the meter pit lid, and eight feet of vertical height above the surface of the preceding
               described area in an unobstructed condition. Any plant material, earth, landscaping
               material, fencing material, decorations, fixtures, or structures within or intruding
               upon the preceding described area that prevents or unduly hinders meter servicing,
               or that endangers the health or safety of city personnel servicing the meter shall
               be deemed an obstruction for purposes of this section of this article. A property
               owner shall promptly remove any obstruction upon receipt of notice from the city of
               such condition.
(c)
For replacement of a water meter vault, a property owner receiving water service shall
               maintain an area, accessible from the public right of way, over and above the meter
               vault encompassing a surface area measured not less than six feet outward from the
               center of the meter pit lid, or such area as the city may determine to be the safest,
               most economical and feasible for replacement of a meter vault, and ten feet of vertical
               height above the surface of the preceding described area in an unobstructed condition.
               Obstruction shall have the same meaning set forth in subsection (b) of this section.
               A property owner shall promptly remove any obstruction upon receipt of notice from
               the city of such condition.
(d)
For routine servicing of water meter pits, a property owner receiving water service
               shall maintain an area, accessible from the public right of way, over and above the
               meter pit encompassing a surface area measured 24 inches outward from the center of
               the meter pit lid, and three feet of vertical height above the surface of the preceding
               described area in an unobstructed condition. Obstruction shall have the same meaning
               set forth in subsection (b) of this section. A property owner shall maintain such
               area in an unobstructed condition at all times, and in any event shall promptly remove
               any obstruction upon receipt of notice from the city of such condition.
(e)
For replacement of a water meter pit, a property owner receiving water service shall
               maintain an area, accessible from the public right of way having the following dimensions:
               a rectangle of four feet by six feet, oriented for the safest, most economical and
               feasible means for replacement of the water meter pit, and six feet of vertical height
               above the surface of the preceding described area in an unobstructed condition. Obstruction
               shall have the same meaning set forth in subsection (b) of this section. A property
               owner shall promptly remove any obstruction upon receipt of notice from the city of
               such condition.
(f)
Where no physical impediment prevents city access to the meter, meter pit, or meter
               vault, but the property owner, agent of the property owner, tenant, or occupant none
               the less denies access or prevents access by the city, such action shall be deemed
               a denial of access and shall subject the property owner or user of the city water
               service to the fees and actions provided in
section 102-62.3
of this article irrespective of any absence of physical barriers to access.
(g)
The utility manager shall have discretion in the strict application of the above standards
               and requirements for access and he or she may make reasonable modifications thereto
               on a case by case basis when it can be demonstrated that access to the meter, meter
               pit, or meter vault can be accomplished without strict application of the standards
               set forth herein, that the safety and welfare of the city personnel performing the
               work will not be endangered, that the alternative standard is economically reasonable,
               that the modification to the standard under consideration is feasible and practical
               and the modification to the standard will still permit the accomplishment of the desired
               work. A request for modifications of the standards may be made by the property owner,
               or may be initiated at the utility manager's request. In the absence of information
               satisfactory to the utility manager in his or her professional judgment that a modification
               of the standard meets all criteria set forth herein and is justified, the standards
               set forth in this section shall apply.
(
Ord. No. 4030, § 1, 10-16-2006
)
